Mutation

/myoo-TAY-shun/ — rhymes with station · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A mutation is a change in an organism's genetic material that can produce a new or different trait.

A rare mutation gives these tulips their striped petals.

Worked Example

In the laboratory, a scientist observes that a population of fruit flies has developed a new eye color never before seen; further testing reveals a change in their DNA that caused this entirely new trait.

Mutation is more precise than 'change' because it specifically refers to a genetic alteration in DNA that produces a new hereditary trait — that biological and hereditary component is essential to the meaning.

How Mutation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

variation

variation: a small, natural difference within a group

modification

modification: a deliberate change made to something existing

adaptation

adaptation: a change helping something suit its environment

Antonyms

stability

stability: the state of staying steady and unchanged

constancy

constancy: the quality of remaining faithfully the same

How Strong Is It? — variation → modification → adaptation → mutation

variation vs. mutation

variation vs. mutation: Variation is the mildest of these words — a slight, ordinary difference — while a mutation is a genuine change written into an organism's genetic code.

modification vs. mutation

modification vs. mutation: A modification is stronger than a variation but still gentler than a mutation; it is an adjustment made to something, whereas a mutation rewrites the underlying blueprint itself.

adaptation vs. mutation

adaptation vs. mutation: An adaptation comes close to a mutation in force — it is a real change that helps a living thing survive — but a mutation is the deeper genetic shift that can create such new traits in the first place.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of mutation.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mut

Root — mut: to change (Latin)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or process of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: The Latin root mut- means 'to change,' and the suffix -ation names an act or process — so a mutation is literally 'the process of changing,' which is exactly what happens when genetic material shifts and produces a new trait.

Use the root in a new word: mutant

Use the root in a new word: mutant: In the comic, the mutant turtle gained his strange powers when his genes suddenly changed — a mutant is literally 'one who has changed.'

Root Check

Word Choice

scientific / technical

Mutation is a precise scientific term for genetic changes that produce new traits in organisms. Use it when discussing heredity, evolution, or genetics. For everyday changes in appearance or form, 'alteration' or 'change' is more natural and appropriate.
